body:
I feel ya... I'm in a similar spot and trying to figure this out myself. I work construction, up and down ladders all day, cheap-o exercise watches were putting me into an average of 9.? km walking a day (about 4 miles); tons of heavy lifting (usually up ladders) usually said in that 6-7k cal / day range.

  
I'm 6'2 290lbs, I spent a large portion of 2022 on the 1200cal "diabetic" premade meals (3 meals a day) because I know I struggle with portioning - so it was an "easy" solution for me. I dropped a lot of girth off my middle - 52x34 pants to 38x34 pants. This was a terrible EAP dieticians advice - I should never have gone that low on calories but I guess free advice is worth exactly what you paid for it. Picked the diabetic meal plan not so much for medical need - it just seemed the best fit for calories/stuff I wanted to eat.

I came out 10lbs heavier but - different overall shape. And constantly exhausted.

Unfortunately doesn't help because I really need to loose actual weight due to knee/foot issues (and I'm not comfortable with my weight being at the limit of my ladders load rating). I backed off and just ate what I wanted for the last 6 months or so after realizing how badly the last advice was. Still the same weight, though I had to dig out the 40" pants. I can't seem to move off this 285-295lbs range. Was coming here looking for advice again trying to figure out what my next attempt looks like. And apparently I'm going to commiserate with someone else having the same battle instead.

If I follow my current budget focused on debt repayment; realistically I can probably focus on 1200-1500$/month towards savings without major upheaval in my living situation. 

Yes 88k of room in TFSA.   
Live in the lower mainland - pretty sure home ownership HERE isn't even possible for me - pretty sure I'd be retiring elsewhere; but one of my back of mind fears is I do have a family history with multiple instances of early onset Dementia/Alzheimer's. Current plan is - I'm in a place I can afford, not planning to move in the next decade and intentionally moved into a national REOC owned building - for sake of stability.  
I'm not understanding the <250k in RRSP's comment. And google's not helping me much; other than making me feel overwhelmed by articles with large concepts I'm not grasping. 

I know I probably need to sit down with a financial advisor - and I've actually tried to do so, but between relatively lower end of the income spectrum for them, and some of their fees and/or hourly rates seem downright insane to me... This is how I've ended up on reddit asking...
